messages:
maria: quick sync — running AWQ vs GPTQ bakeoff on new-llama2-13b-q. seeing perplexity regressions on long-context evals concentrated around mid-encoder layers (~20-26). attaching per-channel KLD heatmap (gist).

kevin: can you paste the top KLDs? rough thresholds?

maria: quick snip: 
```
layer 22 channel 137 KLD 0.82 (baseline 0.07)
layer 22 channel 142 KLD 0.71
layer 25 channel 3   KLD 0.65
```

simon: those are huge. likely heavy-tailed activations breaking the per-channel scale in AWQ. what's the activation skew/kurtosis?

maria: heavy positive tail. kurtosis ~18 on channel 137, repeats of numeric tokens and dates seem to amplify it.

kevin: two quick mitigations to try: 1) per-channel percentile clamp before quantize, 2) per-layer fallback (FP16) if too many channels flagged. propose gating: KLD>0.25 OR kurtosis>12 -> per-channel clamp; if flagged_channels_in_layer > 12 -> layer FP16.

maria: ran a quick patch: applied 99.95 percentile clamp and re-quant AWQ channels only. long-context perplexity down from +6% -> +1.2%. code snippet: 
```python
for ch in channels:
  p = np.percentile(act[ch], 99.95)
  act[ch] = np.clip(act[ch], -p, p)
```

aria: nice. any throughput hit?

maria: none at inference — clamp is applied offline during quantization. throughput identical.

simon: what about soft-skip per-channel (reduce precision) vs full layer FP16? tradeoffs?

kevin: cost model: FP16 for a single layer ≈ 1.9x token compute on our GPU mix vs AWQ layer. If we only fallback for <2 layers, total cost delta small vs user-facing quality improvement.

maria: hybrid test: AWQ everywhere, FP16 for layer 22 and 25 -> perplexity ~baseline +0.2%, latency +8ms/token on our p3-like machines. CPU path unaffected.

repro-bot: reproducibility run started (run_id=run-2147483700-1). artifacts to s3://redwood-quant/runs/2147483700-1

simon: next steps: formalize a gating policy in quant pipeline: metrics (KLD>0.25 OR kurtosis>12) -> per-channel clamp at 99.9-99.99 percentile; if flagged_channels>threshold -> layer-level FP16 fallback. Add evaluation suite with long-context, numeric-stress, codebench, and edge-case prompts.

maria: adding a canary rollout plan for Dedicated: canary=5% traffic with automatic rollback to hosted smaller-variant if downstream quality delta > 2% across canary set.

kevin: can we add a unit test for synthetic heavy-tail inputs so CI catches regressions?

maria: yep, adding "numerics_tail_input.py" that seeds repeated numeric tokens and asserts generation logprob delta <0.5 nats.

aria-ml-bot: PR created: github.com/redwood/quant-protos/pull/455 (summary: channel clamp + layer FP16 fallback + gating tests) :thumbsup:

maria: tagging @eng-platform for canary config. planning to merge staging PR tomorrow and run full bakeoff after.

kevin: nice progress. also consider logging per-channel kurtosis histograms to console and console metrics so SRE/observability can alert when a new model shows unusual heavy-tail activity.

simon: agreed. if we standardize alerts we can catch these before customer impact. thanks all.
